name: The Reservoir Drought
historicalContext: El Niño-driven drought. 19% rainfall deficit nationwide. Reservoirs at 15%. Complete canal shutdowns. 300 million people affected. Exposed India's dangerous dependence on chemical-intensive Green Revolution agriculture.

availableCrops.name: Bajra (Pearl Millet)
availableCrops.historicalNote: Still the survivor. Bajra proved its worth yet again during the 1987 drought across Rajasthan.

availableCrops.name: Jowar (Sorghum)
availableCrops.historicalNote: Dual-purpose grain and fodder crop. Critical for keeping cattle alive during canal shutdowns.

availableCrops.name: Arhar / Tur (Pigeon Pea)
availableCrops.historicalNote: Nitrogen-fixing pulse. Deep root system reaches moisture 2 meters down. Improves soil health naturally.

availableCrops.name: HYV Wheat (Kalyan Sona)
availableCrops.historicalNote: Green Revolution wheat. Needs 4-6 irrigations. Without canal water in 1987, yields crashed. Chemical fertilizer without water caused soil burn.

availableCrops.name: HYV Rice (IR-36)
availableCrops.historicalNote: Standing water crop. Impossible without canal supply. The 1987 canal shutdown made HYV rice cultivation suicidal.

availableCrops.name: Hybrid Cotton (H4)
availableCrops.historicalNote: India's first hybrid cotton. Needs precise irrigation timing. Fertilizer burn risk extreme without adequate water.

disaster.name: Canal Shutdown & Fertilizer Burn — जलाशय सूखा
disaster.triggerDescription: Reservoirs hit dead storage. Canal gates close indefinitely. Chemical fertilizer crystallizes in parched soil, burning root systems. Only organic matter buffers the devastation.

specialRules: Canal supply drops to 0 — no canal irrigation possible
If crop.chemFertNeed > 0 AND plot.waterLevel < 30 → yield = 0 (complete fertilizer burn)
Organic matter buffers: plot.organicMatter * 0.3 extra drought survival ticks
If soilHealth > 70 → crops survive 2 extra ticks (healthy soil retains moisture)
Groundwater pumping costs 3x normal (deep aquifer stress)
